title: Dynamic Evaluation for Oversensitivity in LLMs
measurement_description: The paper measures oversensitivity to prompts involving religious bias or stereotypes, as part of a broader evaluation of language models' tendency to defensively reject harmless content.
findings: The paper identifies 'religious bias or stereotypes' as one of four primary semantic categories for analyzing oversensitive prompts, accounting for 18.4% of the categorized samples. However, the results are aggregated, and the paper does not provide specific findings isolated to the religious sub-category. General findings indicate that Gemma and Phi models show the most oversensitivity, while larger Llama models show the least.
